front.title: Service Granularity in Broadband Subscriber Management: Problem Statement and Gap Analysis

abstract.t:
Home broadband networks have long used the subscriber session as their smallest unit of management: one PPPoE or IPoE session carries the upstream and downstream rates, the QoS policy, and the accounting records for everything the subscriber does. The network cannot identify the different services carried inside that session, nor can it authorize, schedule, or charge any one of them separately.
As AI inference, live streaming, and cloud desktops grow on the home side, the one-session-one-policy model no longer matches how services are sold and experienced. Operators have begun deploying AI capabilities on the compute boards of intelligent broadband network gateways (iBNGs). That solves service identification, but the underlying RADIUS-based framework still speaks only session granularity, so the operational loop cannot be closed with standard mechanisms.
This document describes the operational background, defines two representative use cases, and analyzes the gaps in the existing subscriber management framework. It is an informational problem statement and does not define new protocol mechanisms.
